name: Sunder Chase
description: Sunder Chase is a seasonal event that occurs during the summer rather than the fall season.

log.summary: Sunder Chase was referenced as a seasonal event associated with summer, contrasting with the current fall season.
notes: Referenced as a seasonal event that occurs during summer rather than the current fall season.

log.summary: Session discussion clarifies how the Sunder Chase works at Haven Hold: throwing a gauntlet into Hanzuni's hoard triggers the race, with contestants first selecting any number of magical hoard items as pre-race prizes before running the circuit. Items knocked overboard during the chase return to the hoard, non-winners forfeit everything taken, and only the winner permanently keeps chosen treasures. Walker learns he may need another completed circuit to obtain certain Haven magic items, though Quaylin notes he can borrow cash directly from the Haven Hold dragon without racing. The party also recalls a previous dispel magic attempt during a Sunder Chase that ended badly.
notes: Completing another circuit may be required to obtain certain magic items in the Haven.
Haven Hold's dragon hoard is set up as a pre-race prize pick before running the circuit.
Throwing a gauntlet into Hanzuni's hoard at Haven Hold triggers a chase to claim treasure.
Contestants choose any number of magical hoard items before racing.
Items lost overboard during the race return to the hoard; non-winners lose all taken items back to the hoard.
Only the winner permanently keeps chosen hoard treasures.
Quaylin says Walker can borrow cash directly from the Haven Hold dragon without racing.
The party recalls a previous dispel magic attempt during the Sunder Chase that went badly.

log.summary: Carlkin calls Sunder Chase a death race. He and Benji trace their friendship, and the argument over who had the idea, to when it first started; Benji claims he gave Carlkin the idea. The party won it, and Carlkin says he gave them some guidance. Ord's contribution was dispelling magic on another ship. Typical tactics are cannons, faster sails, or burning ships; a dragon simply flying faster than a ship is the other route. Riding Araden is now considered cheating and would disqualify a rider, since Araden flies faster than an average ship. Another copper dragon, still around and distinct from Araden, is now a hoard dragon for the race.
